description: AI/ML techniques for microsecond-scale trading including order book modeling, latency optimization, market microstructure learning, and adaptive execution algorithms.

techniques.name: DeepLOB Order Book Modeling
techniques.description: Convolutional + recurrent architecture for predicting short-term price movements from limit order book snapshots. Proposed by Zhang et al. (2019). Captures spatial structure of LOB levels and temporal dynamics.
techniques.verification_notes: DeepLOB paper confirmed on arXiv. AUC scores of 0.70-0.75 are consistent with reported results. GitHub implementation available.

techniques.name: RL Optimal Execution
techniques.description: Reinforcement learning for minimizing market impact during order execution. Learns adaptive strategies outperforming TWAP and VWAP benchmarks by 5-15 basis points.
techniques.verification_notes: RL for optimal execution is well-documented. Basis point improvement varies by market and order size.

techniques.name: GAN Synthetic Order Flow Generation
techniques.description: Generative adversarial networks for creating realistic synthetic order flow data for strategy testing and augmentation. Addresses scarcity of labeled HFT training data.
techniques.verification_notes: GAN-based financial data generation is an active research area.

techniques.name: FPGA/ASIC Hardware Acceleration
techniques.description: Custom hardware (FPGAs, ASICs) for sub-microsecond ML model inference in HFT. Knowledge distillation and model quantization reduce model complexity for deployment on specialized hardware.
techniques.verification_notes: FPGA-based inference for HFT is established practice at major firms (Citadel, Two Sigma, Jane Street).

techniques.name: Online Learning / Adaptive Algorithms
techniques.description: Continuously adapting algorithms that update without full retraining, essential for non-stationary HFT environments. Includes online gradient descent and bandit algorithms.
techniques.verification_notes: Online learning for financial applications is well-documented in market microstructure literature.
